transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I've gotten so strict about what and how much I eat that I'm barely eating at all lately. It's starting to really interfere with my work on my painting job sites, which is why I'm here today.
Do you feel that your current weight or body shape is a significant problem, or are you worried that you might gain weight even though you are eating very little?

Honestly, I don't see my weight as a problem because I feel like I'm just in "job shape" to move around tight scaffolding easily, and my family is overreacting. But I am absolutely terrified of gaining weight; even just thinking about eating something like pizza after work gives me a rush of panic that I'll look bigger in my overalls.
Have you noticed any physical changes due to your restricted eating, such as your menstrual periods stopping or feeling unusually cold all the time?

I haven't really noticed feeling cold or had issues with my periods, but I've definitely lost weight since my pants hang off me and my tool belt needs new holes. I also get really lightheaded and almost blacked out on a ladder recently, though I honestly just thought I was exhausted from working so hard.

Do you ever feel like you lose control over your eating and consume an unusually large amount of food in a short period, or do you ever use methods like self-induced vomiting or laxatives to prevent weight gain?

No, I’ve never lost control or eaten a lot like that, and I definitely don't throw up or use laxatives. It's actually the exact opposite—I exert extreme control to restrict my food as much as possible, constantly calculating calories. Even the thought of eating something heavy like pizza makes me panic, so I just avoid it entirely.
